## Proof

- Move the Windows timing-sensitive scenario into a private library unit test. A per-worker thread-local one-shot ready/resume event carries the real opened directory/receipts/lock identities and paths. It means handles are open, not that the lock was acquired. The original persist implementation runs without copied write logic.
- Drop the fixture lock File and short-lived identity probes before attempting rename while the worker remains paused, so the fixture cannot manufacture refusal with extra no-delete directory handles.
- Both refusal and success paths preserve original directory identity, exact two-receipt bytes/objects/index mappings, public readback and no redirection. Original sentinel/no replacement index/restore checks remain. Same-path rename must succeed after all handles are released; only after every proof may errno5/32 be accepted.
- Existing CI --lib runs a dedicated one-case native unit subprocess with an exact filter. The parent checks actual count 1 and success; native child command, phase identities, count and safety outcome are printed. No Linux cfg exclusion/zero tests is Windows acceptance.
- The integration target additionally exercises the non-test public library: two-node persistence, complete index/readback and same-directory identity rename/restore after handle release. All other original integration scenarios remain byte-identical.
